post.title: Would You Have Stopped? #shorts
post.description: Sam is sure he would have stopped. Almost everyone is. In Stanley Milgram's 1963 Yale study, 40 men were told to give 'shocks' to a learner (an actor — no real shocks) for every wrong answer. Psychiatrists predicted only about 1 in 1,000 would go all the way; 26 of 40 (65%) went to the maximum 450 volts when the experimenter told them to continue. In later variations (Milgram, Obedience to Authority, 1974), when two fellow 'teachers' refused, only 4 of 40 went to the end. Critics such as Gina Perry (2012) note that many participants doubted the shocks were real. #psychology #shorts #milgram #obedience
